notes: kb/Work PB5247 landed. §1985:XIII.3.19.4 GR1 sizes the sum counter by the category of the SUM entry: a. numeric, the item's size and decimal point (PicInfo.Digits and the receiver scale); b. numeric edited, its digit positions and decimal point (PicInfo.DigitPositions); c. alphanumeric or alphanumeric edited, "the size of that data item, excluding any editing characters, or 18 characters, whichever is smaller, and the sum counter is an integer". ReportSectionBinder.SumCounterDigits computes the three arms, the c. arm capped at 18 below COBOL-2002 (the 2002 text, §2002:13.16.52.3 GR1, dropped the cap), and SumFamilyOf builds the counter with PicInfo.SumCounterItem (signed, scale 0 for c.). Witnesses: 1985-GR-XIII_3_19_4-1 (numeric 9(3)V9, edited ZZ9.9 and X(4) totals) and pb5247_alphanumeric_sum_counter_18_digits (an X(20) entry: an 18-digit counter holding 2, moved as [000000000000000002  ]).

next.reason: 1985: "If the associated data item is alphanumeric or alphanumeric edited, the size ... or 18 characters, whichever is smaller, and ... an integer"; 2023: "derived from the corresponding number of digits, excluding insertion editing characters, in the PICTURE clause". Both define a signed numeric sum counter sized from the item's digits. 2023 no longer has the alphanumeric/alphanumeric-edited case with its 18-character limit and integer result.
